title: 76 Preliminary study on animal science students experiences with practical goat management sessions
content:
Abstract
During the Fall of 2024 at the Goat Farm / MAFES H.H. Leveck Animal Research Center a class was held for students of Animal Science, including talks and hands-on activities. Topics covered included biosecurity, handling facilities, goat breeds, research at the farm, pasture management, fencing, animal welfare, buck characteristics, and farm management, students gained practical experience with FAMACHA© scoring, body condition assessment, and hoof trimming. The study aimed to analyze the association between gender, background in animal science or farming, and various measures of satisfaction and practicality in a survey of 31 participants of 135 Animal Science students from Animal and Dairy Sciences Department at Mississippi State University. Data was analyzed using the Proc Freq and Chi Square (SAS, 9.4). The demographics showed that 90.32% of participants were female and 9.7% were male. Regarding background, 29.0% had no background in animal science or farming, 45.2% in animal science, and 25.8% in farming. The relevance of the information was rated as “Very Relevant” by 67.7% of participants and “Relevant” by 32.3%. The usefulness of the information was rated as “Very Useful” by 64.5%, “Useful” by 32.3%. In terms of agreement with the information presented, 48.4% agreed, 35.5% strongly agreed, and 16.1% were neutral. The clarity of the information was rated as “Very Well” by 41.9%, “Well” by 38.7%, and “Somewhat” by 19.4%. The informativeness was rated as “Very Informative” by 38.7%, “Informative” by 48.4%, and “Somewhat Informative” by 12.9%. The applicability of the information was rated as “Very Applicable” by 61.3%, “Applicable” by 29.0%, and “Somewhat Applicable” by 9.7%. The importance of the information was rated as “Very Important” by 64.5%, “Important” by 29.0%. The practicality of the sessions was rated as “Very Practical” by 67.7%, “Practical” by 25.8%, “Somewhat Practical” by 3.2%, and “Not Practical” by 3.2%. Satisfaction with the hands-on activities was rated as “Very Satisfied” by 54.8%, “Satisfied” by 22.6%, “Somewhat Satisfied” by 19.4%, and “Not Satisfied” by 3.2%. Overall satisfaction with the sessions was rated as “Very Satisfied” by 61.3%, “Satisfied” by 32.3%, and “Somewhat Satisfied” by 6.5% (Table 1). The results indicated no significant associations between gender and background (P=0.9062), gender and practicality (P=0.6636), gender and satisfaction with activities (P=0.4343), or gender and overall satisfaction (P=0.3503). Similarly, no significant associations were found between background and practicality (P=0.1957) or background and satisfaction with activities (P=0.3665). However, there was a tendency towards significance between background and overall satisfaction (P=0.0679). Most hands-on activities were considered highly relevant by the students. However, additional data is needed to further improve these practical experiences and ensure a positive and engaging visit for all students at the research unit, especially since for some, this was their first encounter with small ruminants
